The polarity/subscale route pins the reverse-item block {N9_6..N9_9} and the anchor direction, but nothing in the source distinguishes items within a polarity class (e.g. N9_1 from N9_2); that tie rests on the questionnaire's 9.k numbering matching the data's N9_k columns, 11/11. Also, and CORRECTED AT TRIAGE (the round's first account of this did not survive checking): the paper's Table 2 descriptives are not reproducible from the data by any reading, so they were not usable as a matching route and the between-scale correlations were used instead. The round recorded these as 'latent composite scores, not item means'. That explanation fails on the paper's own numbers. Every published SD is 2.0-3.8x smaller than the observed one while the means agree to within 0.3: breadth 3.37/0.29 vs 3.53/0.70, depth 3.01/0.35 vs 2.72/0.73, attentional fragmentation 3.09/0.18 vs 3.30/0.69 -- and an SD of 0.18 for the arithmetic mean of ten 1-5 items with alpha 0.78 is not attainable by any scoring, latent or otherwise (Table 2's own note says 'M, arithmetic mean'). The correlations behave differently again: breadth vs attentional fragmentation reproduces essentially exactly from item means (+0.463 observed vs +0.46 published) while depth reversed gives -0.584 against -0.78. Correcting for unreliability fixes depth and breaks breadth (disattenuated -0.730 and +0.579, alphas 0.749/0.750/0.855), so no single account explains both. What matters for the MAPPING is that this is unaffected: no alternative depth definition fits better (adding 9.10/9.11 raw gives -0.477, reversing 9.6-9.11 gives -0.550, 9.10/9.11 alone give +0.095), the sign and the polarity block still pin the anchor direction, and PARTIAL remains the right status. The unreproducible SD row is a property of the paper, not of this table. instructions are blank because the questionnaire prints none for this block.
